question: A communication satellite acts like a television tower placed at a height of __________ km.
solution:
The correct answer is __**36000 km**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• A **communication satellite** acts like a television tower placed at a significant altitude to facilitate communication over a wide area. 
• The altitude of a communication satellite is generally at **36,000 km above the Earth’s surface**, which is known as a **geostationary orbit**. 
• A satellite in a geostationary orbit appears stationary relative to the Earth’s rotation, ensuring **continuous coverage** of a specific area on the Earth. 
• This orbit is ideal for communication purposes as it allows satellites to cover a large area and provide services like television broadcasting, telecommunication, and internet access. 
• The specific altitude of 36,000 km ensures that the satellite’s orbital period matches the rotation period of the Earth, i.e., 24 hours. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Geostationary Orbit:** 
• Geostationary orbit is located at an altitude of **approximately 35,786 km** above the equator. 
• Satellites in this orbit revolve around the Earth at the same speed as the Earth rotates, making them appear stationary from the ground. 
• This orbit is extensively used for **communication satellites** like television, telecommunication, weather monitoring, and GPS services. 
• **Types of Satellite Orbits:** 
• **Low Earth Orbit (LEO):** Located at altitudes between **160 km to 2,000 km**, used for Earth observation and telecommunication. 
• **Medium Earth Orbit (MEO):** Located at altitudes between **2,000 km to 35,786 km**, often used for navigation satellites. 
• **Geostationary Orbit (GEO):** Located at around **36,000 km**, ideal for communication satellites. 
• **Functions of Communication Satellites:** 
• Provide **television broadcasting**, satellite radio, and internet access. 
• Facilitate long-distance **telecommunication** and mobile services. 
• Enable global coverage for **weather forecasting**, disaster management, and GPS navigation systems. 
• **Examples of Communication Satellites:** 
• **INSAT series:** India’s communication satellites used for television broadcasting and meteorological purposes. 
• **GSAT series:** Another set of Indian communication satellites providing telecommunication services. 
• **Intelsat:** International satellites used for global communication services. 
• **Important Facts:** 
• The concept of geostationary satellites was first proposed by scientist **Arthur C. Clarke** in **1945**. 
• The first geostationary communication satellite was **SYNCOM 3**, launched by the USA in **1964**. 
• India’s first communication satellite was **INSAT-1A**, launched in **1982**. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Why 36,000 km is chosen:** 
• The altitude ensures the satellite’s orbital period matches Earth’s rotational period (**24 hours**). 
• This allows for **stable communication** without the need for constant tracking. 
• **Applications:** 
• Used for **live television broadcasts**, including sports events and news. 
• Critical for **disaster management** and emergency communication. 
• Vital for modern navigation systems and **global internet connectivity**. 
• **Challenges:** 
• High cost of satellite launches and maintenance. 
• Risk of **space debris** affecting operational satellites. 
• Signal latency due to the large distance from Earth.
